nodes.name: Mo foil cleaning
nodes.procedure: The single facet polished polycrystalline Mo foil (10×10×0.5 mm³) was cleaned by cycles of Ar⁺ sputtering (1.5 keV, 10 μA) and UHV annealing (1200 K, 10 min). The cleanliness of Mo foil was confirmed by the absence of carbon and oxygen signals in the subsequent XPS measurement.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Mo-Based Model Catalyst... cleaned by cycles of Ar⁺ sputtering (1.5 keV,10 μA) and UHV annealing (1200 K,10 min)

nodes.name: In situ Mo₂C film carbonization
nodes.procedure: Mo₂C film was first grown on the clean Mo polycrystal by in situ carbonization in an NAP-XPS chamber with 0.3 mbar C₂H₄ while maintaining the sample temperature at 873 K. As the carbonization time increased, two distinct C 1s peaks at 284.5 and 282.8 eV emerged in NAP-XPS spectra, corresponding to graphite carbon and molybdenum carbide, respectively (Figures 1b and S1). Once the intensity increase of the C 1s peak at 282.8 eV from molybdenum carbide reached saturation, the C₂H₄ gas was evacuated and vacuum annealing was performed on the carbonated sample at 1073 K to remove surface graphite carbon. Subsequent UHV annealing resulted in a fading signal of graphite carbon, confirming the successful formation of a Mo₂C film on top of the Mo foil.

nodes.name: Mo₂C thermal oxidation
nodes.procedure: The oxidation-gradient samples were prepared by oxidizing the Mo₂C sample at various temperatures in 0.3 mbar O₂ atmosphere for 10 min. After treatment at 373 K (MCO-373), 573 K (MCO-573), and 673 K (MoO₂).

nodes.name: Mo precursor hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: (NH₄)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O (1g) was dissolved in 20 mL of H₂O and 10 mL of ethanol. The solution was stirred to become clear and then added with 1 mL NH₃·H₂O. Subsequently, dopamine (0.4g) was dissolved in 20 mL of H₂O, and the dopamine solution was added dropwise to the Mo solution and reacted at 313 K for 12 h under continuous stirring. Afterward, the precipitate was collected by centrifugation, repetitively washed with H₂O and ethanol, and lyophilized.

nodes.name: O-Mo₂C powder annealing
nodes.procedure: The O-Mo₂C powder was obtained by annealing the precipitate at 823 K for 5 h under an Ar atmosphere with a temperature ramping rate of 2 K/min.
nodes.source_text: Later, the O-Mo₂C powder was obtained by annealing the precipitate at 823 K for 5 h under an Ar atmosphere

nodes.name: O-Mo₂C/NF ink deposition
nodes.procedure: O-Mo₂C ink was obtained by dissolving 10 mg O-Mo₂C powder in 0.1 mL of nafion, 20 mL of H₂O, and 10 mL of ethanol. Thereafter, the O-Mo₂C ink was added dropwise to the NF which had been ultrasonic cleaned in acetone, HCl, and H₂O sequentially.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo 3d₃/₂ peak at 228.0 eV and C 1s/Mo 3d intensity ratio ≈2.0 confirm formation of Mo₂C film on Mo foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, analysis revealed that the Mo 3d₃/₂ peak appeared at around 228.0 eV, and evaluation of the C 1s/Mo 3d XPS intensity ratio yielded a value of approximately 2.0, further supporting the formation of Mo₂C film...

nodes.characterization_summary: Absence of O 1s signal confirms clean Mo₂C surface free from hydroxyl contaminations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absence of the O 1s signal on the as-prepared Mo₂C surface suggests its freedom from any hydroxyl contaminations (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s peak at 530.0 eV appears after room temperature O₂ exposure; Mo 3d and C 1s signals decrease with increasing oxidation temperature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon exposure to aqueous iodine to O₂ at room temperature, one XPS O 1s peak centered at 530.0 eV begins to appear. Meanwhile, both Mo 3d and C 1s signals decrease.

nodes.characterization_summary: New Mo 3d peaks at 229.0 and 232.5 eV after 573 K oxidation indicate majority MoO₂ presence on MCO-573 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After treatment at 573 K, a pair of new Mo 3d peaks can be observed at 229.0 and 232.5 eV, suggesting a tremendous change in structure and composition...

nodes.characterization_summary: MoO₂ accounts for 21% (MCO-373), 75% (MCO-573), and 100% (MoO₂) in XPS detection ranges based on Mo 3d peak fitting analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wherein we calculate that the corresponding distribution of MoO₂ accounts for 21, 75, and 100% in the XPS detection ranges for samples oxidized at 373 K (MCO-373), 573 K (MCO-573), and 673 K (MoO₂), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: All oxidation-gradient samples show considerably flat surfaces with crystal planes exceeding 10 μm in size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Images acquired using SEM interconnected by vacuum tubes reveal that these samples have considerably flat surfaces with crystal planes exceeding 10 μm in size (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo₂C and MCO-373 show similar surface areas, grain boundaries, and grain sizes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Interestingly, the AFM and larger-scale SEM images of Mo₂C and MCO-373 show these two samples possess similar surface areas, grain boundaries, and grain sizes (Figures S5 and S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance C_dl = ∼0.46 mF/cm² for Mo₂C film and 1.49 mF/cm² for MCO-373 film from CV measurements at different scan rates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: phase-pure Mo₂C film exhibits an ultralow C_dl value (∼0.46 mF/cm²), while the C_dl value of oxidized MCO-373 film is up to 1.49 mF/cm², nearly 2-fold enhancement than the C_dl of Mo₂C film

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band spectra show descending Mo 4d DOS near Fermi level: MCO-373 > Mo₂C > MCO-573 > MoO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2f, the corresponding valence bands... show a descending order for their Mo 4d band density of state intensities near the Fermi level...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo₂C shows O 1s peaks at 531.7 eV (hydroxy) and 530.2 eV (chemisorbed O); hydroxy peak area increases slightly, chemisorbed O substantially with increasing H₂O pressure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While the introduction of 10⁻⁷ mbar of H₂O leads to the emergence of new O 1s peaks, which are deconvoluted into two peaks assigned to hydroxy at 531.7 eV and chemisorbed oxygen... at 530.2 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: MCO-373 shows O 1s oxide peak at 530.0 eV and minor hydroxy at 531.6 eV under 10⁻⁹ mbar H₂O; no significant intensity variation up to 0.1 mbar.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As regards to MCO-373, the O 1s peak under merely 10⁻⁹ mbar H₂O atmosphere can be divided into a main oxide peak at 530.0 eV and a minor hydroxy peak at 531.6 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: MCO-373 O 1s shows decreasing hydroxyl peak intensity from 0.0 V to -0.3 V vs RHE, indicating facile OH* desorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the applied negative potentials increased from -0.1 to -0.3 V, the intensity of the hydroxyl peak decreased significantly, indicating that the OH* intermediates adsorbed on MCO-373 could be easily removed at negative potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo₂C/NF shows Mo 3d peaks at 228.3 and 231.5 eV with no O 1s signal; MCO-373/NF shows new Mo 3d peak at 235.3 eV and O 1s at 530.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The two predominant peaks (228.3 and 231.5 eV) of the Mo 3d XPS profile and the complete absence of corresponding O 1s signal... The new emerging Mo 3d peak at 235.3 eV and the O 1s peak at 530.5 eV confirm the oxidation...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitances C_dl = 30.6 mF/cm² for Mo₂C/NF and 45.0 mF/cm² for MCO-373/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl values of Mo₂C/NF and MCO-373/NF are 30.6 and 45.0 mF/cm² respectively (Figure S26).

nodes.characterization_summary: O-Mo₂C powder shows flower-like morphology with diameters 2-5 μm; uniform deposition on NF confirmed by insets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of the as-prepared initial O-Mo₂C powder... reveal a flower-like morphology with diameters ranging from 2 to 5 μm...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Mo, C, and O elements in O-Mo₂C nanoflowers on NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The insets are SEM images of O-Mo₂C/NF and corresponding EDX mapping, which indicates that Mo₂C nanoflowers are deposited on NF uniformly.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD spectrum of O-Mo₂C/NF shows only metallic nickel peaks, indicating nanoscale dispersion of catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD spectrum of O-Mo₂C/NF only shows the peaks of metallic nickel, indicating the catalyst's nanoscale dispersion (Figure S21).
